items_missed: Never got the caller's name. Asked once, got a garbled answer, and abandoned it — then spent roughly two minutes spelling 'MREDEWING@yahoo.com' back and forth instead. He finished the call not knowing who he was talking to (the caller was not Edmond — 'you can give them a call').
No agenda statement at all. Went from email lookup straight into recapping the estimate; no roadmap, no timeframe, no 'sound good?'
Never listed what's included. Not one word on gas, truck, taxes, insurance, blankets, shrink wrap, bands, or tools — the customer has no idea what the $95-$102/hour actually buys.
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned. Zero insurance content on the entire call — no $2,000 coverage, no 60 cents/lb baseline.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned — no email with the mover's photo and info before the move.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned. Gave an 8:30-9:00 AM arrival window and left it there, with no 'if we miss it we start discounting immediately.'

Clock mechanics half-covered: the 2.5 hour minimum was explained well (because the customer asked), but never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, and never mentioned 15-minute prorated increments after the minimum.

Adjusted the estimate DOWN from 6.5 to 5.5 hours with no stated reason, before seeing any inventory — on a 4th-floor unit with a shared elevator, a second elevator out of service, and 'a bit of a walk' to the door. The access facts he had just collected argue for more time, not less.
Probed stairs/elevator and walk distance well but never explained them to the customer as time and cost variables in the estimate.
Never asked about a balcony, patio, or storage closet — common on a two-bedroom apartment.

Save Your Ass tips missing. The core message landed but no consolidation examples and no 'take a carload' tip — and the customer had already volunteered she was packing over the weekend to save money, so she was asking for exactly this.
No 'reply with any corrections,' no mention of the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email, and never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'

Never used the customer's name once, and gave no business hours or direct callback number — when she asked whether she could send the walkthrough to the number she'd called, he redirected to email without answering the question.
top_strength: Two things stand out. First, the probe on access was textbook and better than most calls we grade: he asked whether the 4th-floor elevator was shared or reserved, how far the unit sits from the elevator, learned a second elevator is out of service, confirmed the destination is single-story with curbside driveway access, and asked specialty-item questions by name ('any appliances, antique safe pool tables, pianos'). Second, the booking close was the best moment on the call — rather than letting a pending virtual walkthrough stall the sale, he held both dates: 'I can put you down for the third, fourth and then Monday whenever we do the virtual walkthrough we can make those adjustments... at least you have those two days locked down already. So they can't be taken up by anybody else... If that's fair.' He paired it with 'we don't require deposit or credit card info to get on our schedule' and 'I'll send over a confirmation email with all the details,' and walked away with two dates booked, a Monday 10 AM walkthrough, and a confirmed callback number. He also delivered the prep lever cleanly — 'anything you do ahead of time only helps cut the timing cost... you only pay for what you need us for' — and it visibly changed her behavior: she came back with 'we're trying to pack some of this stuff over the weekend just to kind of keep the cost down.'
coaching_note: Sergio, you sold the price and skipped the value — that's the whole 7/20 in the pricing section. You quoted $95 and $102 per mover per hour and never told her what those dollars include, so she has nothing to compare against the cheaper guy who quotes $85 and bills her for fuel and tape. Fix it with the full block, every call: 'That rate covers everything — the truck, the gas, taxes, insurance, all the blankets, shrink wrap, straps and dollies, and the tool bag for any disassembly and reassembly. No credit card fees, no fuel surcharge, no stair fees. You're also covered by our No Worries Damage Coverage up to $2,000 per move, handled in-house by our own claims team, not a third-party insurer. A few days before the move I'll email you your mover's photo and a short bio so you know exactly who's showing up. And we back an On-Time Guarantee — if we miss your window, we start discounting immediately.' That paragraph is roughly 45 seconds and it's the highest-value 45 seconds on the call. Second priority, and this one matters to estimate accuracy specifically: you cut the estimate from 6.5 to 5.5 hours without a reason, right after learning she's on the 4th floor, sharing one working elevator, with a walk to the unit. Those facts push time up. If you're going to move an estimate, say why out loud, and let access facts move it in the direction they actually point — a low estimate you have to blow through on move day costs us more than an honest one. Third, cheap and immediate: get the caller's name in the first thirty seconds and use it three or four times. You finished a 14-minute booking call without ever knowing who you'd been talking to.
phone_presence_notes: Polite, patient, and competent — apologized during the email spelling confusion and reassured her with 'for sure, yeah' and 'no worries' — but wholly transactional: no name use, no humor, no empathy markers, and the customer drove nearly every question herself.
